> Could you please try the following steps:
> 
> * Resume the last checkpoint and make sure the nan persists
> * Resume from the last checkpoint and step save frequency to 1
> * Resume from the last checkpoint and make sure nan immediately appears in the following step
> * Add a breakpoint in the ppo_actor loss function and print old_log_probs, log_probs and ratio to find out which part in the loss computation causes nan.

Hello, after careful analysis, I found that the issue lies in the calculation of `low_var_kl`. In the problematic step, the loss has normal values (without NaN or Inf), but during backpropagation, the `exp` operation in `ratio = torch.exp(kl)` within `low_var_kl` （https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/8cae42dc29736d0802ded43c5ecf67a809d56bd8/verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py#L386）causes extreme values, leading to NaN in `kl`. My temporary solution is to use `torch.clamp(kl, min=-5, max=5)` to constrain `kl` before computing `ratio`. **This approach works, but I feel uncertain about it. Could you kindly help confirm whether this is an appropriate solution?**

Welcome to read and quote our article. We have proven that in GRPO, the k2 loss is an analytical expression, which is better than the k3 loss. When the model generates a low probability, the gradient of the k3 loss will experience exponential growth, causing the model to collapse. However, the k2 loss does not have this problem. We have also provided additional correction methods for off-policy and std in GRPO.

中文：目前不建议把这个 issue 当作已解决关闭。#789 只是在 `grad_norm` 非有限时跳过更新，属于防止异常权重更新的保护措施，并不能证明 `!` 输出 / KL NaN 的根因已经修复。相关 #891 仍是 open，评论里也有用户反馈 clamp、关闭 KL 或关闭 vLLM V1 并不总是有效。

当前 main 相对 2025 年 3-4 月已有一些相关变化：`low_var_kl/k3` 会在 `exp` 前 clamp `ref_logprob - logprob`，文档也支持 `low_var_kl+` / `k3+`，用于保持 k3 前向值但用 k2 梯度做 straight-through。建议先在最新 main 或最新 release 上确认是否仍复现，并说明使用的是 `low_var_kl`、`low_var_kl+`、`mse/k2` 还是关闭 actor KL loss。
